title: Measured hip excursion in unilateral hip osteoarthritis

sources.attribution: Bertaux et al., Scientific Data (2022). Public gait data and metadata, CC BY 4.0.

method: Plug-in Gait hip flexion/extension (HipAngles_X) range, max minus min in degrees. HOA includes the affected side before surgery. HEA includes asymptomatic controls.

All 101-point hip angle waveforms under multiple cycle labels in a trial-side were identical. Each distinct trial-side counts once. Average trials within side, available sides within person, then people within cohort.

Cycle uses the full normalized gait cycle. Loaded stance requires a matched ipsilateral GRF trace on the identical 101-sample time grid with peak at least 60 in the archive's normalized units and one interior contiguous contact above 5% of that peak lasting 40–80% of the cycle. Phase edges and partial contacts are excluded. Loaded-stance excursion omits the brief low-force ends of stance.

Matching pairs a control with a patient of the same sex and age within three years without replacement. Among maximum-cardinality matchings, minimize total absolute age difference. 10,000 seeded percentile bootstrap resamples of people, or fixed pairs for matched contrasts.

Controls and patients differ in other characteristics, including body mass and walking speed. Requiring a complete interior contact preferentially selects the limb whose stance falls inside the exported stride. Force completeness restricts the loaded-stance subset. Findings concern preoperative OA and asymptomatic gait, without patient-level gluteal tendinopathy labels.

observedGait.method: Two experienced physicians rated frontal and sagittal gait videos. The public metadata give one consensus code per patient and visit.
observedGait.scope: Labels describe visible gait patterns within the preoperative OA cohort. Concurrent gluteal tendinopathy was not assessed in the archive.

publishedStance.source: Allison et al., Gait & Posture (2018), Table 2
publishedStance.scope: Independent symptomatic cohorts and a different gait-lab protocol. The Bertaux force-gated interval approximates stance. Patient-level classification requires independently labeled GT and OA recordings.
